⭐ History of modern Komunno ⭐

In 1894, Kommuno adopts the "Golfen constitution" establishing an autocratic monarchy where power is shared between Victor Zimo, third regional worker party leader, Igornof Kommodik and a parliamentary assembly. Igornof Kommodik his the nephew of the General Landen, who command the army. But Kommodik quickly came into conflict with the parliamentarians, then in power 19th 1896, in suspending the pre-constitution and granting himself full powers with the help of the General Landen. In septembre 4th 1896, he restored the military regime.
During the 1914-18 world war, the state of Kommuno remained neutral, but during the 1939-45 war, it attacked the Sultanate of Al-Dosum, taking control of it for almost 85 days. The territory is renamed the Republic Islamic of South komunno and given as a gift to the powerful Prince Mohammed Bin Ïssã in terms of alliance. In may 8th 1947, the Treaty of Gregonof was signed and the Colonel Taylor J. Landen, grand-son of Gen. Landen became the new Komunno leader.

Colonel Landen regime makes it a sort of "tyrannical dictatorship" where he deports millions of revolutionaries who are left to die of cold and starvation, when it is not the army itself that shoots them when they try to resist; it happens that others are locked up in hangars that are made to work assembling military equipment or making Cordone flags and banners.

In december 2000, the lifting of the visa requirement for peoples of Kommuno wishing to travel to countries outside the Cordone region represents a first concrete step towards its integration.

The crisis, during which Kommuno plays a major role in the reception and transit of WA troops, marks a turning point in political relations.

Embracing autarky has reduced access to Irak mineral ressources and South Komunno oil, but the Komunnaritan economy has more or less survived the transition. However, in the distant nation of Canada economic activity was formerly almost entirely dependent on selling coffee to Komunno, leaving them with crippling unemployment, tens of thousands in poverty, and an imminent famine.
